intro: Subir means to go up, to climb, to get on (a bus) or to rise (prices, temperature). It's an irregular -ir verb: the u changes to o in tu, ele and eles of the present (sobes, sobe, sobem). Everything else is regular.

presente.pt: Eu [subo] as escadas todos os dias.
presente.en: I climb the stairs every day.
Are you going up by lift or on foot?
The temperature rises a lot in summer.
We go up to the castle on Sundays.
Prices go up every year.

perfeito.pt: Ontem [subi] a serra com uns amigos.
perfeito.en: Yesterday I climbed the hills with some friends.
Did you go up the Belém Tower?
They went up to the room.

imperfeito.en: When I was a child, I used to climb trees.
You always used to take the stairs up.
The bus was going slowly up the street.
We used to run up the hill.

futuro.en: I'll go up to the top floor.

futuro.pt: Amanhã a temperatura [subirá] para trinta graus.
futuro.en: Tomorrow the temperature will rise to thirty degrees.
We'll climb the mountain on Saturday.
Prices will go up again.

condicional.pt: Eu [subiria] a pé, mas estou cansado.
condicional.en: I would walk up, but I'm tired.
Would you climb onto the roof?

condicional.pt: Ela [subiria] a montanha, se tivesse tempo.
condicional.en: She would climb the mountain if she had time.
We would go up by lift.

presente.en: I always take the stairs up.
The price is going up.
Do you often go up to the castle?

perfeito.en: We went up to the third floor.

imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to climb trees.
The road went up to the village.
imperfeito.pt: A estrada subia até à aldeia.

imperfeito.en: They always went up by lift.

futuro.en: I'm going to go up now.
The temperature is going to rise.
We're going to go up to the top.

condicional.en: I would go up, but there's no lift.
condicional.pt: Eu subiria, mas não há elevador.

condicional.en: Would you climb that mountain?
Prices would go up.

notes.presente: Stem change: u becomes o in sobes, sobe, sobem (like fugir: foges, foge, fogem). Eu subo and nós subimos keep the u.
notes.perfeito: Subir a = to go up to / to climb (subi ao castelo). Subir para = to get on or into (subir para o autocarro).
notes.futuro: In everyday speech you'll mostly hear ir + infinitivo: vou subir, vamos subir, os preços vão subir.

patterns.en: to go up to the first floor

compare.ex: Subo de elevador, mas desço pelas escadas.

recap: Quem sobe também tem de descer. (Whoever goes up also has to come down.)

intro: Descer means to go down, to come down or to get off (a bus or train). It's a regular -er verb with one spelling change: eu desço (the ç keeps the soft c sound before o).

presente.en: I'm getting off at the next stop.
Are you coming down with me?
The river runs down to the sea.

presente.pt: Nós [descemos] a pé até à praia.
presente.en: We walk down to the beach.
Are you coming down now or later?

perfeito.pt: [Desci] do autocarro em frente ao museu.
perfeito.en: I got off the bus in front of the museum.
Why did you come down so fast?
The temperature dropped during the night.
We walked down the street to the river.

imperfeito.pt: Todos os dias [descia] as escadas a correr.
imperfeito.en: Every day I used to run down the stairs.
The sun was slowly going down.
We used to go down to the beach after lunch.
They always got off at the same stop.

futuro.en: I'll come down in five minutes.

futuro.pt: O preço da gasolina [descerá] no próximo mês.
futuro.en: The price of petrol will go down next month.
We'll get off in Coimbra.
Will you go down the stairs?

condicional.en: I would come down, but it's raining.
Would you go down a black ski run?
He would get off at the next stop.

condicional.pt: Eles [desceriam] à praia, se fizesse sol.
condicional.en: They would go down to the beach if it were sunny.

presente.en: I'm getting off here.
The road goes down to the beach.
presente.pt: A estrada desce até à praia.

presente.en: The temperature is dropping.

perfeito.en: We got off the train in Porto.
Did you come down the stairs?

imperfeito.en: We used to go down to the river.
He always got off at that stop.
The children ran down the street.
imperfeito.pt: As crianças desciam a rua a correr.

futuro.en: I'm going to come down now.
The temperature is going to drop.
Where are we going to get off?

condicional.en: I would get off here.
Would you go down by lift?
They would come down later.

notes.presente: Spelling: eu desço. The ç keeps the soft 's' sound before o. Descer de = to get off: descer do autocarro, descer do comboio.
notes.perfeito: For -er verbs, nós is the same in the present and the perfeito: descemos (we go down / we went down). Context tells you which.
notes.futuro: Everyday Portuguese prefers ir + infinitivo: vou descer, vamos descer.

patterns.en: to get off the bus / the train
to go down to the beach
to get off at the next stop

compare.ex: Subo de elevador e desço a pé.

recap: Desço do autocarro e desço a rua até ao rio. (I get off the bus and walk down the street to the river.)

intro: Dormir means to sleep. It's irregular only in eu durmo (o becomes u); all other forms follow the regular -ir pattern.

presente.en: I sleep eight hours a night.
Do you sleep well in this hotel?
The baby sleeps a lot.

presente.pt: Ao fim de semana, [dormimos] até tarde.
presente.en: At the weekend we sleep in.

presente.pt: Os miúdos [dormem] no quarto ao lado.
presente.en: The kids sleep in the room next door.

perfeito.en: I slept really badly last night.
We slept in a hotel near the beach.

imperfeito.pt: Quando era pequeno, [dormia] com a luz acesa.
imperfeito.en: When I was little, I used to sleep with the light on.
When I arrived, she was already asleep.
On holiday we used to sleep until midday.

imperfeito.pt: Os meus avós [dormiam] sempre a sesta.
imperfeito.en: My grandparents always had an afternoon nap.

futuro.pt: Hoje [dormirei] em casa da minha irmã.
futuro.en: Tonight I'll sleep at my sister's.
You'll sleep better with the window open.
We'll sleep on the train.
They'll sleep at a campsite.

condicional.en: I would sleep more if I could.
Would you sleep in a tent?
He would sleep all day.
With this noise, we wouldn't sleep.

presente.en: I can't sleep.
The baby is sleeping.
I sleep badly when it's hot.

perfeito.en: We slept at a friend's house.
perfeito.pt: Dormimos em casa de um amigo.

imperfeito.en: I used to sleep with the window open.
Everyone was sleeping.
She always had a nap after lunch.
imperfeito.pt: Ela dormia sempre a sesta depois do almoço.

futuro.en: I'm going to sleep.
Where are we going to sleep?
You're going to sleep here.

condicional.en: I would sleep all day.
Would you sleep in a tent?
They would sleep better here.

notes.presente: Only eu changes: durmo. The same happens in cobrir (cubro) and tossir (tusso). Going to bed is deitar-se: Deito-me às onze.
notes.perfeito: The classic morning question: Dormiste bem? Answers: Dormi muito bem / Dormi mal / Não dormi nada.
notes.imperfeito: Dormir a sesta = to have an afternoon nap. For 'was sleeping' at a moment, EP usually says estava a dormir.

compare.en: to go to bed / to lie down
compare.ex: Deito-me às onze, mas só durmo à meia-noite.

recap: Durmo mal quando bebo café à noite. (I sleep badly when I drink coffee at night.)

intro: Acordar means to wake up (Acordo às sete) and also to wake someone up (Acorda-me às sete). It's a regular -ar verb. In Portugal it's used without -se.

quick.en: Wake me up at seven, please.
What time do you wake up?

presente.en: I wake up at seven every day.
What time do you wake up on Saturdays?
The baby wakes up during the night.
We wake up early to go to work.
The neighbours always wake up very early.

perfeito.en: Today I woke up with a headache.
Did you wake up in time?

perfeito.pt: [Acordámos] às seis para apanhar o avião.
perfeito.en: We woke up at six to catch the plane.

imperfeito.en: I used to wake up without an alarm clock.
You always used to wake up in a good mood.
My mother used to wake us up with music.
On holiday we used to wake up late.

futuro.en: Tomorrow I'll wake up earlier.
He won't wake up before ten.

futuro.pt: [Acordaremos] às cinco para ver o nascer do sol.
futuro.en: We'll wake up at five to see the sunrise.
Will you wake up in time?

condicional.pt: Eu nunca [acordaria] tão cedo a um domingo.
condicional.en: I would never wake up so early on a Sunday.
Would you wake me up at eight?
Without an alarm clock, he wouldn't wake up.
They would wake up later if they could.

presente.en: I wake up at seven.
Wake me up at eight, please.
The baby is waking up.

imperfeito.en: I used to wake up early.
She always woke up in a good mood.
We used to wake up without an alarm clock.

futuro.en: I'm going to wake up early tomorrow.
Are you going to wake me up?
They're going to wake up late.

condicional.en: I would never wake up at five.
Would you wake me up at seven?
We would wake up earlier.

notes.presente: In Portugal acordar has no -se: Acordo às sete. Getting out of bed is a different verb, levantar-se: Acordo às sete e levanto-me às sete e meia.
notes.perfeito: EP spelling: acordámos (we woke up) vs acordamos (we wake up). Brazil writes both without the accent.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Amanhã vou acordar cedo.

patterns.en: to wake up with the alarm
to wake up in a good mood
to wake up with a headache

compare.ex: Acordo às sete, mas só me levanto às oito.
Adormeci às duas e acordei às sete.

recap: Acordo às sete, mas só me levanto às sete e meia. (I wake up at seven but only get up at half past seven.)

intro: Vender means to sell. It's a regular -er verb. You'll see 'Vende-se' on signs for things that are for sale.

quick.en: How much are you selling this for?

presente.pt: [Vendo] a minha bicicleta por cem euros.
presente.en: I'm selling my bike for a hundred euros.
Do you sell second-hand books?
This shop sells fruit and vegetables.

presente.pt: Nós [vendemos] bolos no mercado ao sábado.
presente.en: We sell cakes at the market on Saturdays.
They sell houses in the Algarve.

perfeito.en: I sold the car to my neighbour.
Have you sold the flat yet?
The company sold a lot this year.
They sold everything in two hours.

imperfeito.pt: Quando era estudante, [vendia] roupa numa loja.
imperfeito.en: When I was a student, I sold clothes in a shop.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [vendia] peixe no mercado.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather used to sell fish at the market.
We used to sell lemonade in the summer.
In the old days, they sold newspapers in the street.

futuro.en: I'll sell the house next year.
He'll never sell the boat.
We'll sell the tickets online.
Will you sell the old car?

condicional.pt: Eu não [venderia] esta casa por nada.
condicional.en: I wouldn't sell this house for anything.
How much would you sell your phone for?

condicional.pt: Ele [venderia] mais com um site melhor.
condicional.en: He would sell more with a better website.

condicional.pt: Nós [venderíamos] a casa, se fosse preciso.
condicional.en: We would sell the house if necessary.

presente.en: They sell coffee here.
I'm selling my car.
presente.pt: Estou a vender o meu carro.

presente.en: Do you sell stamps? (polite)

imperfeito.en: My grandmother used to sell flowers.
We used to sell fruit at the market.
They didn't sell newspapers there.

futuro.en: I'm going to sell my computer.
Are you going to sell the house?
They're going to sell the tickets tomorrow.

condicional.en: I would never sell this ring.
Would you sell that book?
They would sell more online.

notes.presente: Signs: Vende-se (for sale), Aluga-se (for rent). Vender a alguém = to sell to someone.
notes.perfeito: For -er verbs, nós is the same in the present and the perfeito: vendemos (we sell / we sold).
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vou vender o carro.

patterns.en: to sell for a hundred euros

compare.ex: Vendi o carro velho e comprei um novo.

recap: Vende-se casa com vista para o mar! (House with sea view for sale!)

intro: Comprar means to buy. It's a regular -ar verb and one of the most useful verbs for shopping and everyday errands.

quick.en: Do you need to buy anything?

presente.en: I buy fresh bread every morning.
Where do you buy your clothes?
She buys the newspaper at the kiosk.
We buy fruit at the market.
Do you buy the tickets online?

perfeito.en: I bought a new mobile phone.

perfeito.pt: O que é que [compraste] no supermercado?
perfeito.en: What did you buy at the supermarket?
We bought a house in Braga.
They bought tickets for the concert.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [comprava] gomas com a minha mesada.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to buy sweets with my pocket money.
Did you use to buy a lot of books?

imperfeito.pt: O meu pai [comprava] sempre o mesmo jornal.
imperfeito.en: My father always bought the same newspaper.
We used to buy everything at the corner grocer's.

futuro.en: I'll buy the presents tomorrow.
He'll buy an electric car.
We'll buy a bigger house.
They'll buy the tickets at the station.

condicional.pt: Eu [compraria] esta casa, se tivesse dinheiro.
condicional.en: I would buy this house if I had the money.
Would you buy a used car?
She would buy everything in this shop.

condicional.pt: Nós [compraríamos] mais, mas é muito caro.
condicional.en: We would buy more, but it's very expensive.

presente.en: I buy bread every day.
Where do you buy your coffee?
We're buying a new sofa.
presente.pt: Estamos a comprar um sofá novo.

imperfeito.en: I used to buy the paper every day.
imperfeito.pt: Comprava o jornal todos os dias.

imperfeito.en: We used to buy fish at the market.
She never bought anything.

futuro.en: I'm going to buy a present.
Are you going to buy the tickets?
We're going to buy a house.

condicional.en: I would buy that dress.
Would you buy a used car?
They would buy more if it were cheaper.
condicional.pt: Eles comprariam mais, se fosse mais barato.

notes.presente: Ir às compras / fazer compras = to go shopping. Comprar a alguém = to buy from someone (Compro o peixe ao senhor do mercado).
notes.perfeito: EP spelling: comprámos (we bought) vs compramos (we buy). Brazil writes both as compramos.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vou comprar pão.

patterns.en: to buy a present for someone

compare.ex: Comprei o casaco e paguei com cartão.

recap: Comprei pão, fruta e um presente para a minha mãe. (I bought bread, fruit and a present for my mother.)

intro: Aceitar means to accept. It's a regular -ar verb, used for offers, invitations, payment methods and situations you simply have to accept.

presente.en: I accept the invitation with great pleasure.
Would you like a glass of water?
The restaurant doesn't take cards.
We accept your proposal.

presente.pt: Eles não [aceitam] reservas ao fim de semana.
presente.en: They don't take bookings at the weekend.

imperfeito.en: I used to not accept criticism.
My father never accepted help.
We used to accept everything they gave us.
They only accepted cash.

futuro.en: I'll accept the decision.
Will you accept the challenge?
Will the bank accept the request?
They'll never accept these conditions.

condicional.pt: Eu [aceitaria] o emprego, mas é longe.
condicional.en: I would accept the job, but it's far away.
Would you agree to work on Sundays?
He would never accept that.
We would gladly accept.

presente.en: Do you take card?
I accept your apology.
She doesn't accept help.

imperfeito.en: They only accepted cash.
She always accepted our invitations.
imperfeito.pt: Ela aceitava sempre os nossos convites.

imperfeito.en: My grandmother never accepted gifts.
imperfeito.pt: A minha avó nunca aceitava presentes.

futuro.en: I'm going to accept the offer.
Are they going to accept?
We're going to accept the decision.

condicional.en: I would accept, but I can't.
Would you accept a coffee?
He would never accept that.

notes.presente: Aceitas um café? is a polite, friendly way of offering something. Aceitam cartão? is the question to ask before paying.
notes.perfeito: In Portugal the past participle is usually aceite (Brazil: aceito): O cartão não foi aceite. The perfeito is regular: aceitei, aceitámos.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vou aceitar a proposta.

patterns.en: to accept a proposal / an offer

compare.ex: Recusei o convite, mas aceitei o café.

recap: Aceitei o convite e aceitaram o meu cartão! (I accepted the invitation and they took my card!)

intro: Resultar means to result (from) or, very often in Portugal, to work / to be effective: Não resultou (It didn't work). It's a regular -ar verb, mostly used in the 3rd person.

presente.en: This medicine works really well.

presente.pt: O problema [resulta] da falta de comunicação.
presente.en: The problem results from a lack of communication.
These tricks always work.
With children, shouting doesn't work.
The pronunciation exercises really work.

perfeito.en: An agreement came out of the meeting.

imperfeito.en: This method used to work.
I tried everything, but nothing worked.
Grandma's remedies always worked.
Telling the dog off never worked.

futuro.en: Do you think it will work?
This plan will work, I'm sure.
The new timetables will work better.
More work will come out of this change.

condicional.en: That would never work.
A calm conversation would work better.
Those ideas would work in a bigger company.
With more time, the project would work.

presente.en: It doesn't work.
This trick always works.
Does it work?

imperfeito.en: Nothing worked.
That method used to work.
Shouting never worked.

futuro.en: It's going to work.
Do you think it's going to work?
This idea isn't going to work.

condicional.en: That would never work.
Would it work?
It would work better with more people.

notes.presente: Resultar is the natural EP way to say a plan, trick or method works. For machines use funcionar: O elevador não funciona. Resultar de = to result from; resultar em = to result in.
notes.perfeito: Resultou! and Não resultou. are very common reactions when you try something.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vai resultar, vais ver!

patterns.en: to work with someone (Com ele não resulta.)

compare.en: to pay off / to get results

recap: Tentei de tudo e finalmente resultou! (I tried everything and it finally worked!)

intro: Reconhecer means to recognise (a face, a voice, a place) and to acknowledge or admit something. It's regular apart from the spelling of eu reconheço.

presente.en: I recognise this voice.
Do you recognise that man?
He admits it was a mistake.
We acknowledge your effort.

presente.pt: Os meus amigos [reconhecem] logo o sotaque do Porto.
presente.en: My friends recognise the Porto accent straight away.

perfeito.en: I didn't recognise you in that hat!

imperfeito.en: I no longer recognised my street.

imperfeito.pt: O cão [reconhecia] o carro do dono.
imperfeito.en: The dog used to recognise its owner's car.
We used to recognise all the neighbours.
They never admitted their mistakes.

futuro.pt: Daqui a dez anos, não [reconhecerei] a cidade.
futuro.en: In ten years, I won't recognise the city.
You'll recognise the house: it's the blue one.
The boss will acknowledge your work.
We'll recognise the way.

condicional.en: I wouldn't recognise you without a beard.
Would you recognise your primary school teacher?
He would never admit he was wrong.
They would recognise the song straight away.

presente.en: I recognise that face.
Do you recognise me?
I admit it's difficult.

imperfeito.en: I no longer recognised the city.
The dog always recognised me.
They never admitted their mistakes.

futuro.en: You're not going to recognise me.
Are they going to recognise the place?
I'm going to recognise him straight away.

condicional.en: I wouldn't recognise him.
Do you think you'd recognise her?
He would never admit that.

notes.presente: Spelling: eu reconheço (ç before o). Conhecer = to know someone or a place; reconhecer = to identify something you've seen before, or to admit: Reconheço que não sei.
notes.perfeito: Não te reconheci! After não, the pronoun goes before the verb. In a plain affirmative it follows: Reconheci-te logo.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Não me vais reconhecer!

patterns.en: to recognise someone by their voice

compare.en: to know (a person or place) / to meet

recap: Reconheci-te logo pela voz! (I recognised you straight away by your voice!)

intro: Marcar means to mark, but in Portugal it's above all the verb for booking or scheduling: marcar uma consulta, marcar mesa. It also means to score (a goal). Regular -ar verb; note the spelling eu marquei.

quick.en: I'd like to book an appointment.
Let's arrange to meet for coffee.

presente.en: I always book appointments by phone.
Will you book a table for eight o'clock?

presente.pt: Este jogador [marca] muitos golos de cabeça.
presente.en: This player scores a lot of headers.
We book our holidays in advance.
Are you setting the meeting for Monday?

perfeito.en: I booked an appointment at the dentist's.
Have you booked the flight yet?

perfeito.pt: A equipa [marcou] dois golos no fim.
perfeito.en: The team scored two goals at the end.
We arranged a dinner for Friday.

imperfeito.en: I used to write everything down in my diary.

imperfeito.pt: A professora [marcava] os erros a vermelho.
imperfeito.en: The teacher used to mark the mistakes in red.
We used to arrange to meet at the corner café.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [marcavam] sempre golos no fim do jogo.
imperfeito.en: They always scored at the end of the game.

futuro.en: I'll set the meeting for tomorrow.
Will you book the appointment?
Who will score the first goal?

futuro.pt: [Marcaremos] a data do casamento em breve.
futuro.en: We'll set the wedding date soon.

condicional.en: I would book a table earlier.
Would you set up a meeting for Monday?

condicional.pt: Com mais sorte, ele [marcaria] um golo.
condicional.en: With more luck, he would score a goal.
We would book the holidays for August.

presente.en: I always book a table.
Let's arrange to meet for coffee.
He scores a lot of goals.

imperfeito.en: I used to book everything by phone.
The teacher marked the mistakes in red.
imperfeito.pt: A professora marcava os erros a vermelho.

imperfeito.en: He always scored at the end.

futuro.en: I'm going to book the flight.
When are we going to set the date?
Are you going to book the hotel?

condicional.en: I would book it today.
Would you book a table for us?
They would score more with him.

notes.presente: In Portugal, marcar is the everyday verb for booking: marcar uma consulta, marcar mesa, marcar um voo. Reservar is also used, especially for hotels.
notes.perfeito: Spelling: eu marquei (c becomes qu before e). Nós: marcámos with an accent.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vou marcar uma consulta.

patterns.en: to arrange to meet for coffee

recap: Marquei mesa para as oito e consulta para amanhã. (I booked a table for eight and an appointment for tomorrow.)

intro: Apanhar means to catch or to pick up. In Portugal it's the everyday verb for catching transport (apanhar o autocarro), catching a cold, picking things up off the floor, and getting sun or rain. Regular -ar verb.

quick.en: I'm going to catch the train.

presente.en: I catch the eight o'clock bus.
Do you take the metro to work?
The cat catches mice in the garden.
In summer we sunbathe on the beach.
They pick oranges from the tree.

perfeito.en: Did you catch the train in time?

perfeito.pt: Ele [apanhou] a bola com uma mão.
perfeito.en: He caught the ball with one hand.
We got caught in the rain on the way home.

imperfeito.pt: Todos os dias [apanhava] o barco para Lisboa.
imperfeito.en: Every day I used to take the ferry to Lisbon.
As a child, did you collect shells on the beach?

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [apanhava] peixe no rio.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather used to catch fish in the river.

imperfeito.pt: [Apanhávamos] o elétrico para ir à escola.
imperfeito.en: We used to take the tram to school.

futuro.en: I'll catch the first flight in the morning.
Will you take a taxi at the airport?
We'll catch the boat at ten.
They'll catch the train in Porto.

condicional.pt: Eu [apanharia] um táxi, mas é caro.
condicional.en: I would take a taxi, but it's expensive.
Would you take the metro or the bus?

condicional.pt: Com este frio, ele [apanharia] uma gripe.
condicional.en: In this cold, he would catch the flu.
We would take the train if there were one.

presente.en: I take the bus every day.
presente.pt: Apanho o autocarro todos os dias.

presente.en: Pick up the pen, please.
We're catching the train at nine.

perfeito.en: We got caught in the rain.

imperfeito.en: I used to take the tram.
We used to pick oranges.
He always caught the same train.

notes.presente: In Portugal you apanhar transport: apanhar o autocarro, o comboio, o metro, um táxi. Brazil uses pegar for this.

notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vou apanhar o comboio das nove.

intro: Soltar means to release, to let go of or to set loose: soltar o cão, soltar a corda, soltar um grito. It's a regular -ar verb.

quick.en: Let the dog off the lead.
Don't let go of the rope!

presente.pt: [Solto] o cão no parque todas as manhãs.
presente.en: I let the dog off the lead in the park every morning.
Are you wearing your hair down for the party?
The baby lets out shouts of joy.

presente.pt: Nós [soltamos] os balões no fim da festa.

The fishermen release the small fish.

perfeito.en: I let go of the rope by accident.
Why did you let the dog loose?

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [soltava] as galinhas de manhã.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather used to let the hens out in the morning.
We used to let the dog loose in the garden.

futuro.pt: [Soltarei] o cão quando chegarmos à praia.

The judge will release the prisoner tomorrow.

condicional.pt: Eu nunca [soltaria] o cão na rua.

Would you release that fish?

condicional.pt: Ele [soltaria] a corda, se tivesse medo.

presente.en: Let go of my hand!

notes.presente: Soltar is used for letting go of something you hold (soltar a mão), freeing animals or people, and letting out sounds (soltar um grito, uma gargalhada). The adjective is solto: cabelo solto (hair worn down).
notes.perfeito: Soltar-se = to come loose / to break free: O botão soltou-se (The button came off).
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vou soltar o cão.

patterns.en: to let the dog off the lead
to let go of someone's hand / the rope

compare.en: to drop / to let go (very common in EP)

recap: Solta a corda devagar, não a largues de repente! (Release the rope slowly, don't drop it suddenly!)

intro: Crescer means to grow or to grow up. It's a regular -er verb with the spelling change eu cresço.

presente.en: I grow with every mistake I make.

notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: A empresa vai crescer.

futuro.en: I'll post the photos tomorrow.

condicional.pt: Ele [publicaria] o livro, se tivesse uma editora.

presente.en: I post photos every day.

intro: Aperceber-se (de) means to realise or to notice. It's a regular -er verb that is always reflexive and usually followed by de: Apercebi-me do erro. It's very common in Portugal.

presente.en: I'm only now realising the problem.
Do you realise you're late?
He never notices anything.
We notice the mistake straight away.

presente.pt: Os turistas não se [apercebem] do perigo.
presente.en: The tourists don't realise the danger.

perfeito.pt: Ela [apercebeu-se] de que tinha perdido a carteira.
perfeito.en: She realised she had lost her wallet.

imperfeito.en: I didn't notice anything.
He always noticed everything.
We could tell something was wrong.

imperfeito.pt: Os alunos não se [apercebiam] dos erros.
imperfeito.en: The students didn't notice their mistakes.

futuro.pt: Acho que nunca [me aperceberei] da diferença.
futuro.en: I don't think I'll ever notice the difference.
You won't notice a thing.
Nobody will notice the change.

futuro.pt: Os clientes nem [se aperceberão] da diferença.
futuro.en: The customers won't even notice the difference.

condicional.pt: Sem ti, eu não [me aperceberia] do erro.
condicional.en: Without you, I wouldn't have noticed the mistake.
Do you think you would notice the difference?
He would never notice that.
We wouldn't notice anything.

presente.en: I don't notice anything.
Do you realise it's late?
He never notices.

imperfeito.en: Nobody noticed anything.
They noticed everything.
I didn't realise how difficult it was.
imperfeito.pt: Não me apercebia de como era difícil.

futuro.en: You're going to notice the difference.
Nobody is going to notice.
Are they going to realise?

condicional.en: I wouldn't notice.
Nobody would notice.
Do you think you'd notice the difference?
condicional.pt: Achas que te aperceberias da diferença?

notes.presente: Always reflexive and usually with de: aperceber-se de algo, aperceber-se de que... The pronoun follows the verb (apercebo-me) but moves in front after não, nunca, já, só, que: não me apercebo. With nós the -s drops: apercebemo-nos.
notes.perfeito: Não me apercebi = I didn't realise / didn't notice. Very common in Portugal; Brazil would rather say Não percebi or Não me dei conta.
notes.futuro: The table shows the written form, with the pronoun in the middle (aperceber-me-ei). It sounds formal. After não, nunca, que the pronoun goes in front: não me aperceberei. Otherwise use ir + infinitivo: vais aperceber-te.
notes.condicional: Same as the future: written affirmative aperceber-me-ia is formal; after não, nunca, que the pronoun goes first (não me aperceberia).

compare.ex: Reparaste no corte de cabelo dela?
Dei-me conta de que era tarde.

recap: Só me apercebi do erro quando já era tarde demais. (I only realised the mistake when it was already too late.)

intro: Revelar means to reveal or to disclose (a secret, the truth, a result). It's a regular -ar verb. It's also the verb for developing photos: revelar fotografias.

presente.en: I never reveal my sources.

presente.pt: Tu [revelas] sempre o fim dos filmes!
presente.en: You always give away the end of films!

presente.pt: O estudo [revela] que os portugueses dormem pouco.
presente.en: The study reveals that the Portuguese sleep little.

presente.pt: Nós não [revelamos] os dados dos clientes.
presente.en: We don't disclose customers' details.
The results show an improvement.

perfeito.pt: [Revelei] o segredo à minha melhor amiga.
perfeito.en: I told the secret to my best friend.
Why did you give away the surprise?
They announced the name of the winner.

imperfeito.en: I used to develop my photos at home.
Her eyes gave everything away.
We never revealed our plans.
The letters revealed family secrets.

futuro.en: I'll reveal everything tomorrow.
Time will reveal the truth.
We'll reveal the winner at eight.
The tests will reveal the problem.

condicional.en: I would never reveal a secret of yours.
Would you give away the surprise?
He wouldn't reveal her name.
We would tell the police everything.

presente.en: I'm not revealing anything.
The study reveals the truth.
Don't tell anyone!

imperfeito.en: His face gave everything away.
They never revealed their plans.

condicional.en: I would never reveal that.

notes.presente: Revelar sounds a little formal. In conversation you'd often use contar (to tell): Não contes a ninguém! Revelar fotografias = to develop photos.
notes.perfeito: Nós: revelámos with an accent in EP (Brazil: revelamos).
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vão revelar o vencedor amanhã.

recap: Nunca revelo um segredo, nem à minha mãe! (I never reveal a secret, not even to my mother!)

intro: Prever means to foresee, to predict or to forecast. It's irregular and conjugated exactly like ver (to see): prevejo, prevês, previ. You'll hear it a lot in weather forecasts.

presente.en: I expect a lot of traffic today.
What do you predict for the match?

presente.pt: A meteorologia [prevê] chuva para o fim de semana.
presente.en: The weather service forecasts rain for the weekend.
We foresee a difficult year.

presente.pt: Os economistas [preveem] uma subida dos preços.
presente.en: Economists predict a rise in prices.

perfeito.en: I saw this problem coming months ago.
They predicted the end of the crisis.

imperfeito.en: I didn't expect so many people at the party.
The plan included two stops.

imperfeito.pt: [Prevíamos] chegar às dez, mas havia trânsito.

futuro.pt: Com estes dados, [preverei] melhor os custos.
futuro.en: With this data, I'll forecast the costs better.

futuro.pt: O novo sistema [preverá] o tempo com mais rigor.
futuro.en: The new system will forecast the weather more accurately.
We'll allow more time for the journey.

condicional.en: I would never have foreseen something like this.
Would you predict rain with a sky like this?
Who would have predicted this?

condicional.pt: Nós [preveríamos] mais tempo para a viagem.
condicional.en: We would allow more time for the trip.

presente.en: They're forecasting rain.

What do you predict?

imperfeito.en: I didn't expect so many people.

futuro.en: It's hard to predict what's going to happen.

notes.presente: Prever follows ver: prevejo, prevês, prevê, prevemos, preveem. Since the spelling reform, preveem has no circumflex (old spelling: prevêem).
notes.perfeito: The perfeito also follows ver: previ, previste, previu, previmos, previram.
notes.imperfeito: Prever can also mean to plan for or to include: O plano previa uma pausa (The plan included a break).
notes.futuro: Weather talk: A meteorologia prevê chuva. In everyday speech: Vai chover amanhã.

compare.en: to expect / to hope / to wait

recap: Ninguém previu a chuva, mas era de prever! (Nobody predicted the rain, but it was to be expected!)

She always involved everyone.
imperfeito.pt: Ela envolvia sempre toda a gente.

futuro.en: It's going to involve a lot of work.
Are you going to get involved?
We're going to involve the students.

condicional.en: It would involve too much money.
I wouldn't get involved.
Would you involve your boss?

notes.presente: Envolver-se em = to get involved in: Não me quero envolver nisso. Estar envolvido em = to be involved in.
notes.perfeito: Nós is the same in the present and the perfeito: envolvemos. Envolver-se com alguém can also mean to get romantically involved with someone.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Isto vai envolver muito trabalho.

patterns.en: to involve a lot of work

recap: Este projeto envolve muita gente, por isso envolvi-me logo! (This project involves lots of people, so I got involved straight away!)

intro: Fugir means to escape, to flee or to run away. It's irregular in the present: eu fujo (g becomes j), and u becomes o in foges, foge, fogem. The other tenses are regular.

quick.en: I stay away from the heat.

presente.en: I always avoid conversations about politics.
Why are you running away from me?

presente.pt: O gato [foge] quando vê o cão.
presente.en: The cat runs away when it sees the dog.

presente.pt: No verão, [fugimos] do calor de Lisboa.
presente.en: In summer we escape the Lisbon heat.
The thieves escape through the window.

perfeito.pt: [Fugi] da chuva para dentro de um café.
perfeito.en: I escaped the rain into a café.

perfeito.pt: Porque é que [fugiste] da festa tão cedo?
perfeito.en: Why did you run off from the party so early?
The prisoners escaped during the night.

imperfeito.en: As a child, I always ran away from the dentist.

imperfeito.pt: O meu irmão [fugia] sempre das tarefas de casa.
imperfeito.en: My brother always dodged the housework.

imperfeito.pt: [Fugíamos] para a praia ao fim de semana.
imperfeito.en: We used to escape to the beach at weekends.
People were fleeing the war.

futuro.en: I won't run away from my problems.
Will you run away with me?

futuro.pt: O cão [fugirá] se deixares o portão aberto.
futuro.en: The dog will run off if you leave the gate open.
We'll escape the cold in January.

condicional.en: I would run away to a desert island.
Where would you escape to, if you could?
He would never dodge his responsibilities.
With that noise, the birds would fly off.

presente.en: The cat runs away from the dog.
Run!
I avoid crowds.

imperfeito.en: He always dodged the question.
We used to escape to the countryside.
As a child, I used to run away from the dentist.

futuro.en: The dog is going to run away.
I'm not going to run away.
Are you going to escape the cold?

condicional.en: I would run away to the beach.
Where would you escape to?
He would never run away.

notes.presente: Two changes in the present: eu fujo (g becomes j before o) and u becomes o in foges, foge, fogem (like subir). Nós fugimos keeps the u. Fugir de = to run away from / to avoid.
notes.perfeito: The perfeito is regular: fugi, fugiste, fugiu. Nós fugimos is the same in present and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Fugir a = to dodge: fugir à pergunta (to dodge the question), fugir ao assunto (to avoid the subject).
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: O cão vai fugir!

patterns.en: to escape the heat / the rain

recap: Quando vê o cão, o gato foge, mas eu nunca fujo! (When it sees the dog, the cat runs away, but I never run away!)

intro: Indicar means to indicate, to point out, to show (the way) or to recommend. It's a regular -ar verb; note the spelling eu indiquei. Very handy for asking directions.

quick.en: Can you show me the way? (polite)

presente.en: I always recommend this restaurant to tourists.
Can you recommend me a good doctor?
The sign shows the exit.
We show the way on the map.

presente.pt: Os estudos [indicam] que o café faz bem.
presente.en: Studies indicate that coffee is good for you.

perfeito.en: I showed a tourist the way.
Which hotel did you recommend to your parents?
The GPS showed the wrong route.
We gave the address on the form.

imperfeito.pt: Quando trabalhava no turismo, [indicava] os melhores sítios aos visitantes.
imperfeito.en: When I worked in tourism, I used to point visitors to the best places.
The arrow pointed left.
We always recommended the same café.
The signs warned of danger.

futuro.en: I'll put the date on the invitation.
The teacher will tell us which books.

futuro.pt: [Indicaremos] o local da reunião por email.
futuro.en: We'll give the meeting place by email.
The results will show the winner.

condicional.pt: Eu [indicaria] este caminho, é mais rápido.
condicional.en: I would suggest this way, it's quicker.
Which book would you recommend to a beginner?
He would recommend a good restaurant.
We would recommend the north beach.

presente.en: Can you show me the way to the station? (polite)
presente.pt: Pode indicar-me o caminho para a estação?

presente.en: The sign shows the exit.
Everything suggests it's going to rain.

perfeito.en: The GPS showed the wrong road.
perfeito.pt: O GPS indicou a estrada errada.

imperfeito.en: The arrow pointed left.
The signs warned of danger.
He always recommended the same place.
imperfeito.pt: Ele indicava sempre o mesmo sítio.

futuro.en: I'm going to show you the way.
They're going to point out the mistakes.
The teacher is going to recommend a book.
futuro.pt: O professor vai indicar um livro.

condicional.en: What would you recommend?
I would recommend this beach.
That would indicate a problem.

notes.presente: Pode indicar-me...? is a polite way to ask for directions: Pode indicar-me a casa de banho? Tudo indica que... = everything suggests that...
notes.perfeito: Spelling: eu indiquei (c becomes qu before e). Nós: indicámos with an accent.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vou indicar-te o caminho.

patterns.en: to recommend a doctor / a restaurant

recap: Pode indicar-me o caminho para a praia? (Could you show me the way to the beach?)

intro: Valer means to be worth. It's irregular only in eu valho; everything else is regular. You'll use it constantly in phrases like Vale a pena (It's worth it) and Não vale! (That's not fair!).

quick.en: That's not fair! / That doesn't count!

presente.en: I'm worth more than that!
You're worth a lot, don't forget it.
This house is worth a fortune.
Together we're worth more.
These old stamps are worth a lot of money.

perfeito.pt: Os anos de estudo [valeram] a pena.
perfeito.en: The years of study paid off.
Your advice helped me a lot.

imperfeito.en: A euro used to be worth more.
That car was worth a lot of money.

imperfeito.pt: Os conselhos da minha avó [valiam] ouro.
imperfeito.en: My grandmother's advice was worth its weight in gold.
That goal didn't count!

futuro.pt: Esta casa [valerá] o dobro daqui a dez anos.
futuro.en: This house will be worth double in ten years.
Will it be worth waiting?
These coins will be worth a lot in the future.
The effort will be worth it.

condicional.en: It would be worth visiting Porto.
Without you, this wouldn't be worth anything.
Those paintings would be worth millions today.
That ring would be worth a fortune.

presente.en: It's worth it.
How much is this ring worth?
That's not fair!

imperfeito.en: The house was worth a lot.
Her advice was worth its weight in gold.
Money used to be worth more.

futuro.en: It's going to be worth it.
Is it going to be worth it?
futuro.pt: Será que vai valer a pena?

futuro.en: This car is going to be worth more.

condicional.en: It would be worth visiting Sintra.
Would it be worth it?
This painting would be worth a lot.

notes.presente: Only eu is irregular: valho. Vale a pena + infinitivo = it's worth (doing): Vale a pena ver este filme. Não vale! = That's not fair / That doesn't count (in games). Mais vale... = it's better to...
notes.perfeito: Valeu a pena = It was worth it. In Brazil, Valeu! is also slang for 'thanks', but not in Portugal.
notes.imperfeito: Valer is mostly used in the 3rd person: valia, valiam.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vai valer a pena, vais ver!

patterns.en: to be worth a lot / little
to be worth its weight in gold
that's not fair! / that doesn't count!

recap: Mais vale tarde do que nunca, e esta viagem valeu a pena! (Better late than never, and this trip was worth it!)

intro: Terminar means to end or to finish. It's a regular -ar verb, a little more formal than acabar, which is what you'll hear most in conversation.

presente.en: I finish work at six.
What time do you finish today?
The film ends at eleven.

presente.pt: Nós [terminamos] sempre o jantar com um café.
presente.en: We always finish dinner with a coffee.
Classes end in June.

perfeito.en: I finished my degree last year.
Have you finished the report yet?

imperfeito.pt: [Terminava] sempre o dia com um passeio.
imperfeito.en: I always used to end the day with a walk.
The street ended at the river.
We used to finish classes at four.
The dinners always ended with fado.

futuro.en: I'll finish the book this week.
When will you finish your studies?
The building work will end in December.
They'll finish the project on time.

condicional.en: I would finish today if I had help.
Would you finish this by tomorrow?

condicional.pt: Sem aquele golo, o jogo [terminaria] empatado.
condicional.en: Without that goal, the game would have ended in a draw.
We would finish earlier without meetings.

presente.en: Class finishes at five.
I finish work at six.
When does the film end?

imperfeito.en: The road ended at the beach.
We always finished at four.
The party used to end at midnight.

futuro.en: I'm going to finish this today.
When are you going to finish?
The roadworks are going to end in May.
futuro.pt: As obras vão terminar em maio.

condicional.en: I would finish faster with help.
condicional.pt: Eu terminaria mais depressa com ajuda.

condicional.en: Would you finish it today?
They would finish on time.

notes.presente: Terminar and acabar are very close. Acabar is more everyday (Acabei! Acabou-se!), terminar sounds slightly more formal. Terminar com alguém = to break up with someone.
notes.perfeito: Nós: terminámos (we finished) vs terminamos (we finish). Brazil writes both without the accent.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vou terminar isto hoje.

compare.ex: A aula começa às duas e termina às quatro.

recap: A aula começa às duas e termina às quatro. (The class starts at two and ends at four.)

intro: Jogar means to play games and sports: jogar futebol, jogar às cartas. It's a regular -ar verb; note the spelling eu joguei. For instruments use tocar, and for children playing use brincar.

presente.en: I play tennis on Tuesdays.
Do you play football at the weekend?

presente.pt: O meu filho [joga] videojogos a mais.
presente.en: My son plays too many video games.

presente.pt: Nós [jogamos] às cartas depois do jantar.
presente.en: We play cards after dinner.

presente.pt: Os meus avós [jogam] dominó no café.
presente.en: My grandparents play dominoes at the café.

perfeito.en: Have you played this game before?
We played football on the beach.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [jogava] à bola na rua.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to play football in the street.
Did you use to play basketball at school?

imperfeito.pt: O meu pai [jogava] xadrez com o vizinho.
imperfeito.en: My father used to play chess with the neighbour.

imperfeito.pt: [Jogávamos] às cartas nas noites de inverno.
imperfeito.en: We used to play cards on winter evenings.

futuro.en: I'll play in Saturday's tournament.
Who will play in the final?
We'll play against Porto on Sunday.
They'll play at home.

condicional.en: I would play more if I had time.
Would you play in a football team?
He would play all day long.

condicional.pt: Nós [jogaríamos] ténis, mas está a chover.
condicional.en: We would play tennis, but it's raining.

presente.en: Do you play football?
We play cards on Sundays.
The kids are playing football.
presente.pt: Os miúdos estão a jogar à bola.

imperfeito.en: I used to play football in the street.
My grandfather used to play chess.
Did you use to play basketball?

futuro.en: I'm going to play tennis tomorrow.
Who's playing tonight?
futuro.pt: Quem vai jogar hoje à noite?

futuro.en: Are you going to play?

condicional.en: I would play, but I'm injured.
Would you play with us?
They would play better at home.

notes.presente: Jogar = games and sports (jogar futebol, jogar às cartas, jogar xadrez). Tocar = instruments. Brincar = children playing (brincar com bonecas). Jogar à bola is the everyday way to say kicking a ball around.
notes.perfeito: Spelling: eu joguei (g becomes gu before e to keep the hard g). Nós: jogámos with an accent.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Amanhã vou jogar ténis.

recap: Jogo futebol, toco guitarra e brinco com o meu filho. (I play football, play the guitar and play with my son.)

intro: Construir means to build or to construct. It's irregular in the present: constróis, constrói, constroem (with an open ó). Watch the accents that keep the i stressed: construí, construímos, construía.

presente.pt: Eu [construo] móveis de madeira na garagem.
presente.en: I build wooden furniture in the garage.
You build sentences really well!
The council is building a new school.

presente.pt: Nós [construímos] castelos de areia na praia.
presente.en: We build sandcastles on the beach.
Birds build nests in spring.

perfeito.pt: [Construí] uma casa na árvore para os miúdos.
perfeito.en: I built a tree house for the kids.
Was it you who built this?

imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to build huts in the back garden.
The company used to build blocks of flats in Lisbon.

imperfeito.pt: [Construíamos] castelos de areia todos os verões.
imperfeito.en: We used to build sandcastles every summer.
In the old days, they built houses with stone.

futuro.pt: Um dia, [construirei] a minha própria casa.
futuro.en: One day I'll build my own house.
The government will build a new airport.
We'll build a pool in the back garden.

futuro.pt: Eles [construirão] uma ponte sobre o rio.
futuro.en: They'll build a bridge over the river.

condicional.pt: Eu [construiria] uma casa perto do mar.
condicional.en: I would build a house near the sea.
Would you build your own house?
He would build it all by himself if he could.
We would build a cabin in the forest.

presente.en: They're building a hotel.
Birds build nests.
He builds furniture.

perfeito.pt: O meu avô construiu esta casa.

imperfeito.en: They used to build houses with stone.
I used to build huts.
The company was building a bridge.
imperfeito.pt: A empresa estava a construir uma ponte.

futuro.en: They're going to build a school.
We're going to build a house.
I'm going to build a shelf.

condicional.en: I would build a house by the sea.
condicional.pt: Eu construiria uma casa junto ao mar.

condicional.en: Would you build it yourself?
They would build more schools.

notes.presente: Irregular present: construo, constróis, constrói, construímos, constroem. The ó is open, as in avó. Destruir works the same way.
notes.perfeito: The accent on í keeps the i stressed: construí, construíste, construímos, construíram. Only construiu has no accent.
notes.imperfeito: Here too the i is stressed and written with an accent: construía, construíamos, construíam.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vão construir um hotel aqui.

compare.ex: O fogo destrói o que o homem constrói.
Criei uma empresa no ano passado.

recap: O meu avô construiu esta casa com as próprias mãos. (My grandfather built this house with his own hands.)

intro: Destruir means to destroy. It's conjugated like construir: destróis, destrói, destroem in the present, with accents on the stressed í (destruí, destruímos, destruía).

presente.en: I always destroy old documents.
You destroy everything you touch!
Strong sun destroys the plants.

presente.pt: Nós [destruímos] o planeta com tanto plástico.
presente.en: We destroy the planet with so much plastic.

presente.pt: Os miúdos [destroem] os brinquedos num instante.
presente.en: The kids wreck their toys in no time.

perfeito.pt: [Destruí] o castelo de areia sem querer.
perfeito.en: I knocked down the sandcastle by accident.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, eu [destruía] todos os brinquedos.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to wreck all my toys.
The dog used to destroy all the shoes.

imperfeito.pt: [Destruíamos] as cartas depois de as ler.
imperfeito.en: We used to destroy the letters after reading them.
The floods used to destroy the crops.

futuro.en: I'll destroy these papers tomorrow.
The rain will destroy the flowers.

futuro.pt: Se não fizermos nada, [destruiremos] o planeta.
futuro.en: If we don't do anything, we'll destroy the planet.
The machines will knock down the old building.

condicional.pt: Eu nunca [destruiria] uma carta de amor.
condicional.en: I would never destroy a love letter.
Would you destroy the evidence?
A storm like that would destroy the village.

condicional.pt: Nós não [destruiríamos] uma casa tão bonita.
condicional.en: We wouldn't knock down such a beautiful house.

presente.en: The kids wreck everything.
Plastic destroys the sea.
You destroy everything!

imperfeito.en: The dog used to destroy my shoes.
imperfeito.pt: O cão destruía os meus sapatos.

imperfeito.en: Floods destroyed the crops.
We used to destroy the old letters.

futuro.en: The rain is going to destroy the flowers.
futuro.pt: A chuva vai destruir as flores.

futuro.en: They're going to knock down the old building.

condicional.en: I would never destroy that letter.
That would destroy everything.
Would you destroy the evidence?

notes.presente: Same pattern as construir: destruo, destróis, destrói, destruímos, destroem. The ó is open.
notes.perfeito: Accents: destruí, destruíste, destruímos, destruíram, but destruiu has none.
notes.imperfeito: The stressed i carries an accent throughout: destruía, destruíamos, destruíam.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: A chuva vai destruir as flores.

compare.ex: Construí o castelo e o meu irmão destruiu-o.

recap: Em 1755, o terramoto destruiu Lisboa, mas a cidade foi reconstruída. (In 1755 the earthquake destroyed Lisbon, but the city was rebuilt.)

intro: Definir means to define, but also to set or to decide (a date, a goal, a rule). It's a regular -ir verb.

quick.en: We haven't set the date yet.

presente.pt: [Defino] objetivos no início de cada ano.
presente.en: I set goals at the start of every year.
How do you define the word 'saudade'?

presente.pt: O dicionário [define] esta palavra de outra forma.
presente.en: The dictionary defines this word differently.
We set the rules of the game.

presente.pt: Os pais [definem] a hora de deitar.
presente.en: The parents set the bedtime.

perfeito.en: I've already set the date for the party.
Did you set a budget for the holidays?

perfeito.pt: O professor [definiu] o tema do trabalho.
perfeito.en: The teacher set the topic of the assignment.

perfeito.pt: [Definimos] o plano para o próximo mês.
perfeito.en: We decided on the plan for next month.

imperfeito.en: I used to set impossible goals.

imperfeito.pt: O meu pai [definia] as regras lá em casa.
imperfeito.en: My father set the rules at home.
We used to decide the menu the day before.
They used to decide everything in advance.

futuro.en: I'll set the timetables tomorrow.

futuro.pt: A reunião [definirá] o futuro da empresa.
futuro.en: The meeting will decide the company's future.

futuro.pt: [Definiremos] a data do casamento em breve.
futuro.en: We'll set the wedding date soon.
They'll set the rules.

condicional.en: I would set a shorter deadline.
How would you define happiness?
He would decide everything differently.
We would set the price later.

presente.en: How do you define 'saudade'?
We set the rules.
The parents set the bedtime.
presente.pt: Os pais definem a hora de deitar.

perfeito.en: We haven't set the date yet.

imperfeito.en: My father used to set the rules.
imperfeito.pt: O meu pai definia as regras.

imperfeito.en: We used to plan everything in advance.
I used to set impossible goals.

futuro.en: We're going to set the date tomorrow.
Are you going to set a goal?
They're going to decide the prices.

condicional.en: How would you define happiness?
I would set a deadline.

condicional.pt: Eles definiriam isso de outra forma.

notes.presente: Definir is often used for setting or settling things: definir a data, definir um objetivo. The participle is common too: Está tudo definido (Everything's settled).
notes.perfeito: Nós definimos is the same in present and perfeito. Ainda não definimos a data = We haven't set the date yet (EP uses the perfeito where English uses 'have done').
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Vamos definir a data amanhã.

compare.en: to set / to book (a date, an appointment)

recap: Já definimos a data: o casamento é em junho! (We've set the date: the wedding is in June!)

intro: Escolher means to choose or to pick. It's a regular -er verb, essential in restaurants, shops and whenever you make a decision.

presente.en: I always choose the dish of the day.
Will you pick the film tonight?

presente.pt: Ela [escolhe] a roupa com muito cuidado.
presente.en: She chooses her clothes very carefully.

presente.pt: Nós [escolhemos] o destino das férias juntos.
presente.en: We choose our holiday destination together.
The students choose their own books.

perfeito.pt: Ele [escolheu] o vinho para o jantar.
perfeito.en: He chose the wine for dinner.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [escolhia] sempre o gelado de chocolate.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I always chose chocolate ice cream.

imperfeito.pt: A minha mãe [escolhia] a minha roupa.
imperfeito.en: My mother used to pick my clothes.
We used to take turns choosing the films.
They always chose the same table.

futuro.en: I'll choose my course next month.
Which one will you choose?
We'll choose the hotel tomorrow.
The voters will choose the new president.

condicional.en: I would choose the fish.
Which one would you choose?

condicional.pt: Ele [escolheria] a praia em vez da montanha.
condicional.en: He would choose the beach rather than the mountains.
We would choose a house in the countryside.

presente.en: I always choose the fish.
You choose!
I can't choose.

perfeito.en: Have you decided? (waiter, to a group)

imperfeito.en: I always used to choose chocolate.
My mother used to pick my clothes.
imperfeito.pt: A minha mãe escolhia a minha roupa.

imperfeito.en: We used to take turns choosing.

futuro.en: I'm going to choose a book.
Who's going to choose the restaurant?
Are you going to choose?

condicional.en: I would choose the beach.
Which one would you choose?
They would choose a smaller house.
condicional.pt: Eles escolheriam uma casa mais pequena.

notes.presente: Escolhe tu! = You choose! The noun is a escolha (choice): Boa escolha! À escolha = of your choice (sobremesa à escolha).
notes.perfeito: In a restaurant the waiter asks Já escolheram? (Have you decided?). Nós escolhemos is the same in present and perfeito.
notes.futuro: Everyday speech prefers ir + infinitivo: Quem vai escolher o restaurante?

patterns.en: to choose between A and B

recap: Entre carne e peixe, escolho sempre o peixe! (Between meat and fish, I always choose the fish!)
